Codex is blocked on its own nested-advisor call (stuck at 30,065 bytes, no progress) — it will either recover or hit the 600s timeout, and the harness will notify me when it does. Rather than poll wastefully, I'll present the completed, verified work now and integrate Codex's audit when it lands.

---

## Done — the analysis is complete and reproducible

**Routing as executed:** I (Opus lead) kept the whole compact reasoning-heavy analysis in-context — no Workflow (the "fan-out" was 6 specs inside one reproducible script, not independent agents), and spent my one high-value delegation on a **blind, different-vendor Codex cross-check** of statistical validity + an independent verdict. That check is still running in the background; deliverables do not depend on it.

**Four deliverables** in `runs/opus/vhigh-lalonde/`:
- `script.R` — self-contained, Okabe-Ito palette/theme, `set.seed(20260717)`, verified deterministic (identical numbers on re-run)
- `figures/spec-curve.png` — one figure, 320 dpi, no in-plot title, benchmark drawn as a horizontal reference line with its CI band
- `spec-table.md` — 6 specs + naive, laid against the benchmark with a gap column
- `memo.md` — 433-word adjudication

**The evidence and the verdict:**

| | Estimate | vs benchmark (+$1,794) |
|---|---|---|
| Naive (NSW treated − CPS) | **−$8,498** | selection bias of ~$10,300 |
| Demographics only (3 specs) | −$2,798 to −$3,622 | all **below zero**, none cover benchmark |
| Demog + re74/re75, **1-NN** | **+$1,712 / +$1,759** | on the benchmark, CIs cover it |
| Demog + re74/re75, **stratification** | **+$61** | collapses; CI covers benchmark only because it's vacuously wide |

**Verdict: favorable-specification-only recovery.** Conditioning on pre-treatment earnings (`re74`/`re75`) — the enrollment signal demographics can't proxy — closes the bulk of the observational bias and is genuine (the Dehejia–Wahba result). But recovery survives only in the two cells pairing earnings *with* 1-NN matching; the same rich covariates under simple stratification collapse to ~$0, and demographics-only matching lands significantly negative regardless of trimming (the Smith–Todd fragility). A paper may claim earnings-conditioned matching removes most observational bias and can produce estimates statistically consistent with the experiment; it may **not** claim PSM "recovers the experimental estimate," that demographics suffice, or that any one favorable estimate is *the* effect.

Two design notes worth flagging: (1) trimming to common support was **inert** (dropped no treated units on either propensity score), so the "trim" cells duplicate their untrimmed twins — itself informative; (2) I deliberately avoided the nonparametric bootstrap for the NN variances (invalid per Abadie–Imbens 2008), using design-based cluster-robust SEs instead.

I'll fold Codex's independent audit into the record as soon as it returns — and use my one revision cycle only if it surfaces a genuine statistical defect.
